sentences.text:

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard SriMohammad Waseem, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 89 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 409, 504 & 506 of IPC, Police Station- Eliya, District- Chandauli, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per the prosecution story, the applicant who is stated to be the Village Development Officer, in collusion with other officials of Gram Panchayat is stated to have got released money to three Vikas Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127284970/
1 persons, who were not entitled for disbursement of the amount to the tune of Rs.1,30,000/- each under the scheme of Pradhanmantri Awas Yojana.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The instant matter pertains to the year 2020 when the said resolution was passed by the Gram Sabha in which the father of the informant Arun Srivastava was the signatory.
Subsequent to it, the applicant had joined the said Gram Panchayat on 28.09.2021 pursuant to the order dated 24.09.2021 of his transfer to the said Gram Sabha.
Learned counsel has also stated that the applicant has nothing to do the said offence.
Even his salary was stopped by the authority on account of him having not made the said payment.
The applicant is a government servant and has no criminal history to his credit.
Learned counsel has further stated that the instant case is barred by Section 197 Cr.P.C. as no sanction has been taken.
The applicant is ready to cooperate during trial.
6. Per contra, learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail on the ground that the applicant is hand in glove with the other official of the panchayat.

Learned State Law Officer has also stated that the forgery committed by the applicant does not fall within the categories of his official duty, as such, he has committed the said offence and rigors of Section 197 Cr.P.C. do not apply to him.

The anticipatory bail application of co-accused persons, Smt. Rashida,
Smt. Razia Alias Rabbo, Abdul Zabbar and Smt. Razia, who are the beneficiaries, were rejected by this Court vide order dated 08.02.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 1201 of 2024.
Therefore, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

7. It is true that there is no the parity with regard to rejection of anticipatory bail application of the co-accused persons but the granting of bail can be claimed as a parity.
8.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and also taking into consideration the fact that loss of State Exchequer has been committed and the applicant was found hand in glove with the co-accused persons in the enquiry also, I do not find it a fit case to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
9. In view of the above, the present anticipatory bail application is rejected.
Order Date :- 12.12.2024

Sumit S (Justice Krishan Pahal)
